findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at start of inspection. A staff member informed the inspector that the company is responsible for scheduling the course and exam for staff. Two staff members currently present at the facility are awaiting food manager certification. Ensure adequate staff are certified to have at least one CFPM present at all times of food preparation or service.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: A cooked beef steak was observed at the bottom of the prep table cooler without a date mark. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed to ensure that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are date marked after 24 hours, and the beef steak was date marked. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked after 24 hours and discarded after 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the walk-in cooler and the bottom of the prep table cooler. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in the coolers to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of the walk-in cooler and prep table cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager present at the facility during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned to inspector that they had just started working at the facility for the last two weeks and most of the employees in the facility are new as well. PIC was made aware that there needs to be a certified food protection manager present during operational hours at all times. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present in the facility during operation at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to use a barrier after handwashing to avoid recontaminating their hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff bare-handling ready to eat food item(bread). Discussed with PIC and the education on bare handling food was carried out. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to don gloves when handling ready to eat food to prevent contamination through bare-handling ready to eat food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer bucket observed at during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC and a sani bucket was made. Ensure that there is a sani bucket made at all times during food prep.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the caulking on the handwashing sink next to the prep table in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the handwashing sink mentioned will be repaired. Ensure that this sink is caulked to the wall to provided a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed red sauce that has been left out in the counter over night. The corporate policy is 10 hours at room temperature. The facility discarded the old sauce and placed fresh sauce in a new bucket with proper date and time tag. Make every effort to keep food safe by following the standard and requirements of the products served. The violation has been corrected on site. Train employees on red sauce requirements.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.
